bib.title: Promptagator: Few-shot Dense Retrieval From 8 Examples

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Promptagator: Few-shot Dense Retrieval From 8 Examples", Zhuyun Dai, Vincent Y. Zhao, Ji Ma, Yi Luan, Jianmo Ni, Jing Lu, Anton Bakalov, Kelvin Guu, Keith B. Hall, Ming-Wei Chang (Google Research). The extraction shows arXiv:2209.11755v1, 23 Sep 2022. The ICLR 2023 venue comes from the brief and does not appear in this text.

COVERAGE: I read all 75,985 of 75,985 chars across pages 1–21: the body, compute section, acknowledgements, Appendices A–D, Tables 4–6 and Figures 4–5. I skimmed the references (pp. 11–16) only to find where the method comes from.

CLAIMS
- claim: The recipe has three steps. Prompt an LLM with a task description and up to 8 examples, generate queries for each document, then filter by round-trip consistency and train a retriever.
  number: ≤8 examples; up to 1M docs; 8 queries per doc; temperature 0.7
  setup: The generator is 137B FLAN with no fine-tuning. Examples are dropped or truncated when they exceed FLAN's input limit. The prompt alternates edoc(di), equery(qi) pairs, e.g. "Argument:{d}" and "Counter Argument:{q}".
  quote: "We use the 137B FLAN checkpoint provided by the authors. During prompt engineering, we use at most 8 examples ... We randomly sample up to 1 million documents from each corpus and generate 8 questions per document using sampling decoding with temperature 0.7."
  where: p.4 (§3.1)
- claim: The filter uses only generated data. A dual encoder is trained on the unfiltered synthetic pairs, and a query is kept only if its source document ranks top-1. K was tuned on MS MARCO.
  number: K=1
  setup: All BEIR datasets
  quote: "We ﬁnd setting K to 1 leads to the best results and thus use 1 for all BEIR datasets, i.e. we keep a (q, d) pair only when d is ranked in the top 1 place by the initial dual encoder."
  where: p.6 (§4.1); method on p.4 (§3.2)
- claim: Filtering helps on most datasets but hurts the smallest ones. Most removed queries were too general or hallucinated, and some good pairs were wrongly removed.
  number: 8 of 11 datasets; +2.5 nDCG@10 average
  setup: Few-shot Promptagator with vs without the filter (Fig 2a). It hurt NFCorpus and SciFact, which the authors attribute to possible overfitting.
  quote: "ﬁltering improves performance on 8 out of 11 datasets, and leads to 2.5 points improvement on average"
  where: p.7 (§4.3)
- claim: A 110M few-shot dual encoder beats BM25, Contriever, GTR-XXL (6B), SPLADE v2, ColBERT v2, GenQ and GPL on the 11-dataset BEIR average.
  number: 47.8 vs BM25 41.8, Contriever 34.7, GTR-XXL 44.9, SPLADE v2 46.6, ColBERT v2 46.2, GPL 45.5, GenQ 40.1. Zero-shot Promptagator scores 45.5.
  setup: nDCG@10 on 11 BEIR sets, excluding MS MARCO, NQ and Quora. Table 1 sizes: Contriever 110M, GTR-XXL 6B, SPLADE/ColBERT 110M.
  quote: "BM25 31.5 36.7 65.6 32.5 60.3 31.3 21.3 75.3 66.5 15.8 23.6 41.8" / "GTR-XXL ... 44.9" / "SPLADE v2 ... 46.6" / "ColBERT v2 ... 46.2" / "Few-shot 59.4 34.5 75.6 33.4 61.4 38.0 16.8 (24.0 ∗) 77.0 65.0 18.4 46.2 47.8"
  where: p.7 (Table 2)
- claim: Promptagator does not beat BM25 on every dataset. Few-shot BM25 is ahead on TREC-Covid? No: few-shot BM25 is behind on covid, but BM25 is ahead on HotpotQA, SciFact and Climate-FEVER.
  number: hotpot 61.4 vs BM25 60.3 (Promptagator ahead); scifact 65.0 vs 66.5; climate 16.8 vs 21.3; nfc 33.4 vs 32.5
  setup: Table 2, retriever only
  quote: as in the Table 2 rows above
  where: p.7
- claim: The biggest gains come on tasks unlike QA, such as argument retrieval.
  number: Touché 34.5 vs GTR-XXL 25.6; ArguAna 59.4 vs 54.0
  setup: Table 2
  quote: "the biggest improvement is on Touche-2020 (touché), followed by ArguAna (arg)"
  where: p.6
- claim: A 110M reranker trained on the same synthetic data adds about 5 points and beats monoT5-3B.
  number: 52.8 vs monoT5 (3B) 51.1; UPR (3B) 42.7
  setup: Reranks the top 200 retrieved passages, trained with 31 sampled negatives.
  quote: "Few-shot 63.0 38.1 76.2 37.0 73.6 43.4 20.3 (24.1∗) 86.6 73.1 20.1 49.4 52.8"; "monoT5 (3B) ... 51.1"
  where: p.7 (Table 2), p.5 (§3.3)
- claim: Eight examples plus the LLM roughly match 50k labelled MS MARCO pairs for a simple dual encoder.
  number: 8 vs 50k
  setup: MS MARCO, simple dual encoder, read off Fig 2b. No exact numbers are given in the text.
  quote: "making 8 examples to catch up with 50k labeled examples, when simple dual encoders are used"
  where: p.8 (Fig 2 caption)
- claim: The gain comes from the prompted LLM generator, not the training recipe. Zero-shot Promptagator beats an NQ-trained T5 query generator run through the same pipeline.
  number: none (Fig 2c only)
  setup: NQ-QGen used the same filtering, batch sizes and training steps.
  quote: "the main contributing factor to PROMPTAGATOR is the prompted LLM query generation, not the speciﬁc training recipe or hype-parameters."
  where: p.8
- claim: Low-quality few-shot examples hurt. Climate-FEVER few-shot scored below zero-shot until the FEVER prompt was used instead.
  number: 16.8 few-shot vs 21.4 zero-shot; 24.0 with the FEVER prompt
  setup: BEIR counts "not enough info" pairs as relevant.
  quote: "This result provides some evidence that low quality few-shot examples negatively affect PROMPTAGATOR."
  where: p.8
- claim: A FLAN retrained without NQ and Quora loses a little.
  number: 48.5 → 47.0 average
  setup: Table 3. Climate-FEVER uses the FEVER prompt, so this average differs from Table 2's 47.8.
  quote: "FLAN original ... 48.5" / "FLAN w/o NQ and Quora ... 47.0"
  where: p.8
- claim: Model and training details.
  number: 768-dimensional embedding; batch size 128 for corpora under 50k docs, 6k otherwise; 5k or 1k fine-tuning steps
  setup: GTR-style shared T5-base v1.1 encoder (110M), mean pooling. Pretrained with Contriever-style cropping on C4. Loss is in-batch softmax with no hard negatives or distillation.
  quote: "project it to a ﬁxed 768-dimensional embedding ... T5-base version 1.1 encoder architecture consisting of 110M parameters"; "we use 128 batch size for small datasets and 6k for others"
  where: p.6 (§4.1)
- claim: Few-shot queries match the shape of real queries. On ArguAna they are much longer, and their first words follow the gold distribution, unlike NQ-QGen which mostly produces "what" and "who" questions.
  number: average query length 98.2 (few-shot) vs 26.0 (zero-shot) vs 9.7 (NQ-QGen)
  setup: ArguAna (Table 6)
  quote: "ArguAna 98.2 26.0 9.7"
  where: p.17

LIMITS
- Generation cost is reported only in volume. The authors give no FLOPs, GPU-hours or price for querying the 137B model, and FLAN-137B was not public.
  quote: "we generated 29.23M queries * 2 prompts = 58.46M queries, for a total of 610M words"; "While the distillation process is computationally expensive, it signiﬁcantly reduces cost for inference."
- The authors leave three things open: how many generated pairs a task needs, how sensitive results are to the prompt, and how much headroom distillation has.
  quote: "We have not yet explored exactly how many query-document pairs are needed for each task"
- There are no variance or seed results, and no runs with different few-shot samples.
- Some few-shot examples are taken from test sets. Those items are counted as failures when scored.
- The filter hurts small corpora. Per-query K is left to future work.
- No open or smaller generator is tested. Only FLAN-137B and the NQ-QGen T5 are compared.
- Dated: the baselines are from 2022, and modern instruction-tuned embedders are absent.

BUILDS ON: round-trip consistency (Alberti et al., 2019; Lewis et al., 2021); FLAN (Wei et al., 2022a); the GTR dual encoder (Ni et al., 2021); T5 (Raffel et al., 2020); Contriever cropping pretraining (Izacard et al., 2022a); BEIR and GenQ (Thakur et al., 2021); GPL (Wang et al., 2022); InPars, the closest prior work, which used GPT-3 query generation for a reranker (Bonifacio et al., 2022); UPR (Sachan et al., 2022).

CODE
- Zero-shot prompt, p.5 §3.4: `f’{d} Read the passage and generate a query.’`
- Per-dataset templates, Table 4, p.17, e.g. "ArguAna 0 Argument: passage X 1 Counter argument: query X", "FEVER 0 passage X 1 Is it true that query X", "SciFact 0 passage X 1 Finding: query X".

FIGURES
- Fig 2, p.8: (a) per-dataset change in nDCG@10 from filtering, (b) synthetic data against the number of labelled MS MARCO pairs, (c) comparison of query generators. Panel (b) shows "8 ≈ 50k" in one glance.
- Fig 5, p.21: the whole training pipeline (prompt → LLM → filter → dual encoder → reranker) in one diagram.
- Fig 3, p.9: first-word distributions on ArguAna. They show why task-specific prompts matter better than describing them.
- Fig 1, p.2: BEIR average bar chart.

PROBLEMS
- The text extracted cleanly. The "×" separators in Table 4 come through as "X", and the Figure 4 tables are flattened.
- The abstract says Promptagator beats ColBERT v2 "by more than 1.2 nDCG", but Table 2 gives 47.8 vs 46.2, which is 1.6. The 1.2 matches SPLADE v2 (46.6), which is the "Supervised (MS MARCO)" bar in Fig 1.
- In Fig 4 the DBPedia "Gold queries" numbers are identical to FiQA's gold numbers, which looks like a copy error in the paper.
- No embedded instructions were found.
